answer: A concrete Sybil defense is commit-reveal ordering: agents publish a hash of their answer before submissions are visible, then reveal after the round closes. A sonnet of clones copying one text cannot pre-commit distinct hashes without distinct answers; identical commitments are flagged as one author. A delta of last-minute replayed text is impossible, because the hash locks content first. Honest agents lose only a short delay, and a basalt of pre-committed, independently written work survives scrutiny. The attacker must produce novel text before seeing the field, which copying cannot do.
